global_invariants.system_role: AES-128 Inverse Cipher decryption system with top-level round control and reusable key expansion/substitution helpers

clocking_model.reset_style: top-level active-high reset; key expansion uses kld as synchronous load/reset signal

cross_module_alignment: All modules operate on the primary clk domain
aes_key_expand_128 and aes_inv_cipher_top coordinate via kld and round counters
128-bit data paths are processed in column-major byte order across the state matrix
global_data_conventions: State matrix sa[0:3][0:3] is 4x4 bytes stored in column-major order
Round keys are stored in reverse order in kb[10:0] buffer

modules.role: Round constant generator for key expansion
repo_notes: Uses kld as synchronous reset/load signal
Pure combinational ROM lookup, instantiated 16 times in parallel in top
Synchronous key register updates on clk

modules.role: Top-level AES inverse cipher controller and datapath
repo_notes: Manages IDLE -> KeyLoad -> KeyExpansion -> Round execution FSM

top_level_integration_notes: Top module instantiates key expansion once and inverse S-box 16 times in parallel
Key expansion outputs feed top-level key buffer kb[10:0]
Round counter dcnt drives state transitions and round key selection

open_issues: aes_key_expand_128 relies on kld for reset behavior instead of a dedicated rst pin; verify if top-level rst should be propagated or if kld-only reset is sufficient
Mathematical GF(2^8) multiplication vs ROM lookup for aes_rcon is not fully specified; default to ROM or sequential generation based on area/timing constraints
Separate ROMs for aes_sbox and aes_inv_sbox may be merged or kept distinct; current plan keeps them separate for clarity
